parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Build a management system around decisions
parts.body:
ISO/IEC 42001:2023 specifies requirements for an AI management system: policies and objectives, processes to achieve them, maintenance, and continual improvement. Its unit of attention is the organization and its AI activities, not a claim that any particular model is safe. Leadership defines scope and objectives, provides resources, assigns authority, and reviews performance. Teams then connect risk assessment and treatment to operating controls.

Start by defining the boundary. Which business units, acquired products, vendors, and employee uses are in scope? If the inventory excludes a customer service subsidiary, a management-system audit of headquarters cannot tell you how that subsidiary governs AI. Identify interested parties and their relevant needs: customers, workers, regulators, suppliers, and people affected by a decision. Translate these into a policy and measurable objectives.

An ISO management system is a voluntary standard unless an applicable contract or rule makes it a requirement for your organization. Certification, if pursued, examines conformity to specified requirements within an audited scope; it is not legal clearance or a guarantee against harms. Read the licensed standard before claiming formal conformity. ISO's public overview explains the system concept but does not reproduce every normative clause.

example.title: A sensible initial scope
example.body: A bank might cover AI used in customer communication, employee support, and credit operations in two subsidiaries, while documenting why a newly acquired unit is scheduled for a later integration. It should disclose the boundary whenever it describes its management system.

exercise.title: Set the boundary
exercise.body: Write a scope statement naming entities, locations, supplied and purchased AI, and one justified exclusion. List two affected groups whose needs should shape objectives. Identify who approves a change in scope.

parts.label: Design
parts.title: Turn a policy into a control record
parts.body:
A policy saying 'AI must be responsible' cannot be audited or used by a product team. Connect each obligation to an owner, event, evidence, and decision. For a new system, require a record of purpose, excluded uses, affected people, data, supplier, risk assessment, evaluation, approvals, operating metrics, and next review. A change to data, autonomy, audience, or vendor should trigger an explicit review rather than inherit the old approval by default.

Control strength should reflect use and impact. An internal drafting assistant may need data restrictions, sample checks, and an accountable editor. A tool that recommends credit outcomes needs deeper assessment, traceable reasons, monitoring, escalation, and jurisdiction-specific legal analysis. The control record should point to actual test results and responsible people, not contain a row of empty checkboxes.

Make evidence cheap to maintain by linking the inventory to development and procurement workflows. Each record needs a stable identifier and a steward. The CAIO can own the common method, while business leaders own use outcomes and security, privacy, legal, and audit retain their defined responsibilities.

example.title: One change, two reviews
example.body: An internal support chatbot gains access to customer account records. Its owner updates the use record, maps the new data flow, requests privacy and security review, and retests for unauthorized retrieval. The prior approval covered internal policy documents, so it cannot simply be reused.

exercise.title: Build a control record
exercise.body: For a familiar AI use, draft fields for owner, scope, prohibited use, data, model or vendor, evaluation result, approval date, incident contact, and review trigger. Mark the evidence that already exists and the decision blocked by the gaps.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: inventory and accountability

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Use internal audit and management review to improve the system
parts.body:
A management system needs a feedback loop. Set indicators for coverage of the AI inventory, overdue reviews, unresolved high-severity findings, incidents, control exceptions, and benefit against business baselines. Internal audit checks whether the declared process is followed and whether evidence supports its results. It should sample across business lines and levels of risk, including purchased systems and everyday employee use.

Management review is an executive decision forum. Bring changes in business context, legal obligations, supplier concentration, risk trends, audit findings, corrective actions, and resources. Ask whether a control has failed despite apparent procedural compliance. If reviewers routinely rubber-stamp unsafe outputs, more signatures will not fix the problem; change workflow, authority, training, or technology. Assign a deadline and owner to each corrective action, then verify effectiveness on a later sample.

An audit finding should not disappear when a team updates a document. Record the root cause and a test of the revised control. Where another management system already governs security or quality, reuse its evidence and cadence where appropriate, while preserving AI-specific risks and decision rights.

example.title: Trace a control to an executive decision
example.body: Illustrative management-system design, rather than a claim of clause-level ISO conformance: leadership sets an objective that every customer-facing AI service can be paused by an accountable operator within 15 minutes of a severe incident. The risk assessment identifies uncontrolled messages after a model or connector change. The control record names the service owner, pause permission, on-call rota, and quarterly drill. Operating evidence includes a dated drill log, token revocation record, and measured pause time. Internal audit samples 20 services and finds 9 without a named operator. The owner assigns operators, the platform team fixes the pause path, and a later drill tests whether the fix works. Management review sees the coverage trend, residual exposure, and a request for funded on-call capacity. The numbers and target are hypothetical local choices.

exercise.title: Prepare a management review trace
exercise.body: Pick one management-system objective. Link it to a risk, control, owner, operating record, internal-audit test, plausible finding, corrective action, effectiveness check, and an executive resource or risk decision. Label your choices as illustrative until checked against the licensed standard and your organization's formal scope.

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Choose a certification path for the right reason
parts.body:
A leadership team may seek ISO/IEC 42001 certification because customers request independent assurance, procurement asks for it, or the discipline of external review would improve the system. Compare that expected value with the cost of building records, correcting control gaps, and maintaining the audited scope. A badge covering only a small unit can be misleading if most material uses sit elsewhere.

Before commissioning an audit, ask for an internal gap assessment against the actual standard, an inventory coverage check, evidence of controls operating over time, and an executive owner for unresolved findings. Follow one material control through objective, risk, implementation, actual operating record, audit sample, corrective action, and management-review decision. If any link is missing, resolve it rather than polishing a policy. Review how certification interacts with applicable law. An EU high-risk system may have product-specific AI Act duties that a management-system certificate does not discharge. Canadian privacy obligations depend on activity and jurisdiction.

Decide whether to certify now, defer until material gaps close, or run the system without certification and report its performance. Record the scope and limits when speaking to the board or customers. Continue monitoring after any audit; a certificate reflects an assessment at a point and scope, while deployed systems change.

example.title: A staged investment
example.body: A multinational company has a strong central AI policy but cannot locate all subsidiary deployments. It first funds inventory and owner assignment, tests its control record in two business lines, and schedules an internal audit. It will reconsider certification after coverage and corrective-action evidence improve.

exercise.title: Make the assurance decision
exercise.body: Write a short recommendation to a CEO: scope, buyer or regulatory expectation, current evidence gap, cost categories, decision date, and the claim the organization could honestly make today. State what evidence would change your recommendation.
